html:
The Frisians were a Germanic people of the North Sea coast, in what is now the northern Netherlands and northwest Germany. On the map for 600 and 700 they hold the coast from the Rhine mouths to the Weser.

In these centuries they were the great traders of the North Sea. Their boats carried cloth, wine and slaves between the Rhineland, England and Scandinavia, and the market at Dorestad on the Rhine was one of the busiest in northern Europe. They had kings of their own, most famously Redbad, who fought the Franks around 700.

The Franks pushed north step by step. Pepin of Herstal took the southern Frisian lands, and Charles Martel beat them in 734. Missionaries from the Anglo-Saxons followed; one of them, Boniface, was killed by Frisians at Dokkum in 754. By 800 Frisia was part of the Carolingian Empire. Frisian, a close cousin of English, is still spoken there.
sum: The Frisians were a Germanic people of the North Sea coast, in what is now the northern Netherlands and northwest Germany. On the map for 600 and 700 they hold the coast from the Rhine mouths to the Weser.
